title: A long-context generative foundation model for versatile RNA design - Nature Machine Intelligence
byline: Huang; Yanjie; Lv; Guangye; Gao; Ziheng; Cheng; Anyue; Xie; Mengyan; Wang; Zining; Junxi; Ma; Xinyi; Yijun; Xia; Yunpeng; Liu; Weijin; Tang; Yueyang; Shi; Qingy
html:
Abstract

Programmable design of RNA sequences with defined functions remains a central challenge in biology. Despite recent advances, existing RNA generative models lack robust controllable design capabilities and are constrained by short context windows, limiting their capacity to model the complex evolutionary manifold of full-length transcripts. Here we introduce EVA (Evolutionary Versatile Architect), a long-context generative RNA foundation model trained on over 114 million full-length RNA sequences spanning the full breadth of evolutionary diversity. By integrating a mixture-of-experts architecture with an 8,192-token context window, EVA learns a unified, evolution-consistent representation of the RNA sequence space that captures both global transcript structure and fine-grained functional elements. EVA establishes a unified framework for a broad spectrum of RNA design tasks within a single architecture, ranging from mutational fitness prediction to context-aware sequence engineering. We demonstrate EVA’s versatility through de novo design and targeted optimization of diverse RNA classes, including transfers RNAs, aptamers and CRISPR guide RNAs, as well as messenger RNA and circular RNA therapeutics. In wet-lab assays, our best designed aptamers improve both fluorescence intensity and binding affinity by roughly twofold over the positive control. In systematic evaluations, EVA achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven of nine established benchmarks, generating sequences with more than tenfold lower Kullback–Leibler divergence to natural RNA secondary-structure feature distributions than the previous open-source RNA generator.

Data availability

OpenRNA v1 training sequences and the released validation set are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/GENTEL-Lab/OpenRNA-v1-114M. EVA model checkpoints and their associated configurations and tokenizers are available at https://huggingface.co/GENTEL-Lab/EVA. Released benchmark sequence and label files are provided under examples/notebooks/prediction/data/ in https://github.com/GENTEL-lab/EVA. Generated RNA sequences, secondary-structure feature data and codon-optimization results are deposited at https://zenodo.org/records/19027142 (ref. 56). Source data are publicly available on figshare (version 3) at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33473092.v3 (ref. 57). The deposited package contains the consolidated workbook and supporting CSV, JSON and FASTA files, including experimental replicate measurements and Supplementary Table 30 inputs. The accompanying README maps the files to figures and tables and links the associated Zenodo resource at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18786989 (ref. 58. Source data are provided with this paper.

Code availability

The EVA source repository is available at https://github.com/GENTEL-lab/EVA under the Apache License 2.0. Version v1.2.1, including the fixed source archive, is available at https://github.com/GENTEL-lab/EVA/releases/tag/v1.2.1. The v1.2.1 source snapshot is archived on figshare59. The release includes model and tokenizer implementations, generation and scoring tools, supported MoE pre-training, mid-training, fine-tuning and evaluation components, analysis notebooks and fixed reproduction resources. The release also includes the dense-model training script, which we ran to reproduce the corresponding results. The recovered dense-control implementation and validation are available at https://github.com/GENTEL-lab/EVA/blob/v1.2.1/docs/DENSE_CONTROL.md. File-level checksums and manuscript resource correspondence are documented at https://github.com/GENTEL-lab/EVA/blob/v1.2.1/docs/ARTIFACT_PROVENANCE.md. The repository provides installation instructions, versioned resource manifests and a complete representative benchmark workflow, with validation records and per-workflow documentation in docs/REPRODUCTION.md and docs/PAPER_WORKFLOWS.md.
